anomalous transport v2.1.0 (2026-09-05, physics audit docs/pic2d-physics-completeness-audit.md section 4.c, roadmap R1): the v1.4 Bohm hook audited against Brandt et al. 2016 (doi:10.2322/tastj.14.Pb_235, p. Pb_237) and completed with the reference's event model - AnomalousCollisionConfig(alpha, model) with model bohm_perpendicular_rotation (the velocity rotated about the local B by a uniform random angle: v_parallel and |v| unchanged to round-off, gyro-centre shifted 2 r_L sin(phi/2)) beside the v1.4 bohm_isotropic_scattering (the recorded default; every recorded identity unchanged), in the CPU reference (sensitivity.apply_bohm_rotation / rotate_about_field) and the Warp bohm_kernel (mode 1, same Rodrigues operation order). The hook's statistics were already right: exact Poisson probability 1 - exp(-alpha omega_ce dt) per electron per step at the local |B|, elastic (no ledger energy term), count and axial momentum tallied, a separate exact-Poisson process outside the MCC null-collision budget (equivalent to O(nu_an dt x nu_mcc dt)); what the isotropic event lacked was the reference's model (it also randomised the pitch angle). Both events give D_perp = (kT_e/eB) alpha/(1+alpha^2) (Green-Kubo), verified by a diffusion test to 5 % for alpha 1/16 and 0.345 (0.345 sits 10.6 % below the naive alpha kT_e/eB); BOHM_ALPHA_SERIES {1/64, 1/16, 0.345}. alpha = 0 (hook absent) keeps every identity (ss-v4 f10772b25b03 test-pinned); {model, alpha} enter config_sha256. First users: experiments/pic2d_anomalous_transport_v1 (the preregistered alpha-series on the 33 um reference plateau) and the external-validation v0 bohm-0.4 option (amendment 1). See anomalous_transport_v2_1_0

boundaries.anode: z = 0, r < r_bore: Dirichlet U_a (absorbing conductor)
boundaries.channel_wall_and_cone: internal dielectric: masked solid nodes, plasma-side boundary nodes carry the accumulated surface charge; zero field inside (homogeneous Neumann, v1.x closure)

cathode_v2_0.class: CathodeConfig(r_inner_m, r_outer_m, z_start_m, z_end_m, electron_temperature_ev, current_a, current_rule, max_current_a, continuity_relaxation_intervals)
cathode_v2_0.emission: electrons born uniformly in the annulus volume (r^2-uniform, z-uniform) with an isotropic Maxwellian at electron_temperature_ev (the v1.x 2 eV); the Poisson step sees them at the next deposit; born momentum tallied (pz_injected)
cathode_v2_0.position: INSIDE the channel's exit flux tube in the plume (development run attempt 4: r 0.5-2.0 mm, z = L_channel + 0.3-1.0 mm). The first placement - an off-axis annulus in front of the pole face (attempt 3: r 4.5-6.0 mm = 1.5-2 r_exit, z = L_channel + 2-4 mm, the HEMP-T neutraliser position of Kornfeld, Koch and Harmann 2007 / Koch et al. 2011) - did not ignite: event-aware field-line tracing (cft_revival.pic2d.fieldlines, RK2 on the bilinear node field, terminations channel / anode / wall / body / far_field / axis / null) showed the channel's flux tube closes on the front face within ~1.5 mm of the exit (axis null at z = 25.45 mm) and that the annulus sat on pole-face-to-far-field lines (connected fraction 0/24); 95 % of the emitted current left through the far field, I_d -> 0, S fell x15 in 1.1 us. In an electrostatic model without anomalous transport and with a near-collisionless plume, electrons do not cross between flux tubes, so the emission region must lie on lines that enter the bore; it represents the arrival of the neutraliser electrons into the channel-connected tube (the real device crosses the weak-field region by collisions/instabilities the model excludes; Brandt et al. 2016 fed electrons from the far outer boundary at 1 eV in a model with Bohm transport). Declared, fail-closed: cathode.require_channel_connected_fraction (the runner re-traces the region at launch and records the result in summary.json cathode_connectivity)
cathode_v2_0.ignition_gate: stopping_rule.ignition_gate: trailing-window means of S and N_e at declared check times over their reference means after the seed dump (0.05-0.2 us); stop_reason no_ignition (fail-closed) when a check fails; calibrated on v1.3 attempts 1 (failed) / 2 (ignited) and plume attempt 3 - see the protocol note; the contingency if attempt 4 still fails is a declared ignition sequence (exit-plane injection inside the channel for the first N us ramped to zero while the plume cathode carries the current; switch time recorded and excluded from the plateau window), NOT implemented yet

rules.fixed: current_a every step (the v1.x fixed-current rule moved into the plume)
rules.continuity: the emitted current follows the previous series interval's discharge current I_d = e (anode electrons - anode ions)/interval, relaxed by an exponential moving average over continuity_relaxation_intervals intervals and clamped to [current_a (floor = ignition current), max_current_a]; charge conservation of the plasma gives I_cathode = I_d + (I_e - I_i)_far, so in steady state the far-field boundary carries no net current to the chamber. Review section 4.4 variant (c) (Szabo 2001 'injected at a rate which preserved quasineutrality'; Charoy et al. 2019 / Boeuf and Garrigues 2018 cathode-plane injection tied to the current leaving)

neutrals_v2_0.channel_zone: v1.4 0-D inventory over the CHANNEL plasma cells only (volume = channel_volume_m3): feed, exit-aperture effusion, ionisation (channel + plume ionisations both consume channel atoms: the plume atoms are the effused channel atoms), wall/anode ion recycling; ions absorbed on the front face are NOT recycled into the channel (they recombine outside)
neutrals_v2_0.plume_zone: n_g(r,z) = n_g,channel x f(r,z) with f the cosine-law point-source expansion of the channel's effusion flux Phi = n_g v_bar A_exit / 4 from the aperture centre: flux density Phi cos(theta) / (pi rho^2) at distance rho and polar angle theta, divided by the mean speed 3 pi v_bar / 8 of the effusing atoms, gives f = 2 A_exit cos(theta) / (3 pi^2 rho^2), capped at 0.5 (the outgoing half-Maxwellian at the aperture); f = 1 in the channel (free-molecular effusion through an orifice: Bird 1994). Used ONLY as the per-particle MCC probability factor (density_shape) in the null-collision scheme; the plume atoms are not an inventory of their own
neutrals_v2_0.null_collision_ceiling: the MCC null-collision ceiling carries declared headroom above the zero-ionisation density Q/c and the inventory starts at the declared initial_density_per_m3 (= Q/c): with recycling and the artificial relaxation, n_g tracks the rate-based fixed point (Q + R - S)/c, which exceeds Q/c while a seeded ion population drains (R > S) - the plume development run's first launch stopped fail-closed on this at 14 ns with the ceiling AT Q/c. In steady state R <= S bounds n* <= Q/c; the transient is an artefact of the development relaxation and is recorded (max n_g / (Q/c)). The real collision rate is unchanged (probability scale n_g / ceiling); the null-collision cost grows with the headroom (2x: 1.3e-4 per step)
neutrals_v2_0.relaxation_suspension: the artificial relaxation toward n* = (Q + R - S)/c is defined only while a fixed point exists; in any interval with S > Q + R (n* < 0) it is suspended and the inventory follows the conservative balance dn/dt = (Q + R - S - c n)/V alone (NeutralAdvance.artificial_relaxation_suspended; a guard, the v1.3/v1.4 channel runs never reached S > Q + R so their closure is bit-identical). tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_neutral_inventory.py::test_v20_artificial_relaxation_is_suspended_when_ionisation_exceeds_the_sources
neutrals_v2_0.graph_safe_mcc_density: DEFECT FIXED 2026-09-04 (plume attempts 4-5): the v1.4 CUDA-graph step passed the instantaneous MCC neutral density n_g0 x scale as a kernel scalar, which a captured graph freezes at capture time; the MCC therefore ionised at the n_g of the last capture (a particle-array reallocation) rather than the inventory's n_g. Attempt 4: the connected cathode ignited the channel (S 1.4e16 -> 7.3e16 /s in 0.39 us, the continuity cathode following I_d to 7 mA) with S unchecked by the falling inventory until S = 1.26 Q, the relaxation toward the negative fixed point emptied the channel in one 30 ns interval (5.5e19 -> 4.2e18), and the MCC then kept the trough density (S/(n_e n_g) x100 low at an unchanged T_e distribution) so the discharge did not recover when n_g refilled; the ignition gate stopped it at 0.75 us. The density is now a one-element device array read by mcc_kernel (warp_backend.set_neutral_scale copies into it), as the emission rate already was; the direct and graph paths are bitwise while n_g changes every interval (tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_neutral_inventory.py::test_cuda_graph_step_sees_every_neutral_density_update, which fails on the old backend). Affected runs: plume attempts 3-5 only (attempt 3's n_g stayed within 5.6-6.3e19; its cathode-coupling diagnosis stands). gates_v2_0.inherited: peak-node Debye gate, grid-heating triad, omega_pe dt, Courant, Poisson residual contract, neutral inventory bounds - evaluated over the whole L-shaped domain
gates_v2_0.plume_boundary_gate: PlumeBoundaryGateConfig(max_charge_fraction, enforce_after_s, window_steps = 400000, min_accumulated_macro_particles_per_node = 64000) [v2.0.2, 2026-09-04]: at every series record the gate quantity is max over RESOLVED far-field nodes of |<n_i> - <n_e>| / <n_e,peak>, where <.> is the time average over the trailing window of at least window_steps ACCUMULATED steps, read from the SAME window accumulators that produce maps.npz and the frames (sum_t n_e, sum_t n_i on the far-field nodes, DiagnosticAccumulator / the Warp device sums d_n_e, d_n_i) at the series-record host sync - no per-step host sync is added; on the Warp backend the read is two node arrays per record next to the existing charge-map / potential / gate-moment reads. The Simulation keeps cumulative far-field totals that bridge the runner's accumulator resets (a reset increments the backend's diagnostic_generation and the last reading before it is carried; the runner resets right after a series record, so nothing is lost) and a ring of totals per record, so the window is the exact difference of two totals (the frame recorder's construction, frames.interval_maps). The denominator is the mean over the window's records of the instantaneous peak electron density. A far-field node is RESOLVED when its accumulated macro-particle weight over the window, (sum_t n_e + sum_t n_i) V_node / W (macro-particle-steps; = 2 x sample_count_e on a quasi-neutral node), is >= min_accumulated_macro_particles_per_node. The gate is enforced when armed (t >= enforce_after_s) AND the window holds >= window_steps accumulated steps; a violation stops the run fail-closed (PIC2DStabilityError 'plume-boundary gate'). The window history is not checkpointed: after a resume the statistic covers the accumulation since the resume and the gate is enforced again once the window is complete (0.6 us on the plume protocol; disclosed in the record via far_field_window_steps / far_field_window_complete / gate_armed / gate_enforced). Recorded per record: charge_fraction_of_peak (gate quantity), far_field_net_charge_density_max_per_m3, far_field_window_steps / _records / _start_step / _complete / _steps_required, far_field_resolved_nodes, min_accumulated_macro_particles_per_node, far_field_accumulated_macro_particles_max / _median, the unrestricted window statistic over ALL far-field nodes (charge_fraction_of_peak_window_raw, its node and accumulated weight), peak_electron_density_window_per_m3, and the v2.0.1 single-deposit statistic as the shot-noise witness (charge_fraction_of_peak_raw, far_field_raw_max_node, far_field_raw_max_macro_particles). Series arrays plume_far_field_window_steps, plume_charge_fraction_of_peak_window_raw, plume_peak_electron_density_window_per_m3, plume_far_field_accumulated_macro_particles_max; summary plume.charge_fraction_of_peak_window_raw_max, far_field_window_steps_final, far_field_resolved_nodes_final; log column q_far=<gate>(w<steps>/<resolved>n raw <window raw> dep <single deposit>). The far-field potential deviation from exit_v is recorded (Dirichlet: exactly 0). Rationale of the gate is unchanged: a sheath on the box boundary means the box is too small for the beam to leave quasi-neutrally (Brandt et al. 2016).

energy_ledger_correction_v2_0_6.finding: Up to v2.0.5 both backends added the MCC tally's per-MACRO-event threshold energy (n_exc E_exc + n_ion E_ion) e to cumulative['inelastic_loss_j'] WITHOUT the macro weight W, while every other ledger term (kinetic energies, absorbed / injected / born energies, field work, electrode work) carries W. The recorded interval residual (dE_total - accounted sources) was therefore H - (W - 1) L_unscaled ~= H - L_inel with H = interval field work + dU_field - interval electrode work, the true energy created by the field-particle coupling (finite-grid heating is H > 0), and L_inel the W-scaled inelastic power. Recorded inelastic_loss_j / (n_exc E_exc + n_ion E_ion) e = 1 (exactly 1/W of the real loss) on ss-v4, 047, 056 L1, attempts 7 / 8; every recorded residual in the project read too negative by the inelastic power: 7-14 % of the electrode work at the accepted plateaus (v2 base +12.6 %, ss-v4 +10.1 %, 047 +8.0 %, 056 L1 +8.2 %), 25.6 % on attempt 8's last window, 54 % on the ext-val avalanche window (the recorded statistic read -22 % when H was +50 %).
energy_ledger_correction_v2_0_6.identity_and_proof: particle side: dKE(e + i) = field work + injected - absorbed(anode, exit, wall) + born ions - W (n_exc E_exc + n_ion E_ion) e per record. field_work_j IS the summed dKE of the Boris push in both backends, elastic and Bohm scattering preserve speed, the born electron's energy is split from the primary, so the identity is exact up to (i) float round-off and (ii) the MCC's CLASSICAL threshold removal against the ledger's relativistic KE (O(v^2/c^2) of the per-event loss). Measured: |dKE - rhs| <= 1.5e-15 J per record on 7.5e-9 J (CPU), 4.4e-15 J (warp-cpu); the recorded residual equals H to the same round-off; the pre-v2.0.6 bookkeeping misses by the whole W-scaled loss (test_particle_side_identity_closes_to_round_off_and_the_residual_equals_h). On a well-resolved, field-free, strongly collisional box (0 V / 0 V, 20 eV seed on 1e22 m^-3 Xe, lambda_D 0.6 mm on 167 um cells) the corrected residual is -0.01 ... -0.03 % of the inelastic loss while the pre-v2.0.6 statistic reads -100 % of it (test_corrected_residual_is_zero_on_a_no_heating_collisional_box...). Post hoc on the recorded runs: sum(H - recorded) equals (W - 1) x the recorded unscaled loss to 7e-5 ... 9e-5 relative on every ignited discharge (the classical/relativistic mismatch at 10-30 eV; 1.2e-3 on the no-ignition attempt 3 whose collisions are at hundreds of eV), and the count-based per-record correction from ss-v5 L1's series.jsonl agrees with H to 3.4e-5 of max|H|.

poisson_gmg_v1.operator: the v1.x/v2.0 masked cylindrical finite-volume node operator unchanged (mesh.py conductances epsilon_0 A / l with the 2 pi r weighting; unknowns = plasma nodes minus Dirichlet anode / exit / far field / grounded body conductor; homogeneous Neumann into the dielectric solids with the accumulated surface charge; Dirichlet couplings moved to the right-hand side by poisson.apply_operator exactly as the block-Thomas paths); no permittivity map exists in the model, so none is coarsened
poisson_gmg_v1.hierarchy: vertex-centred coarsening by two in r and z (an axis with an odd cell count keeps its last node: 90 x 720 -> 46 x 361 -> 24 x 181 -> 13 x 91); coarse unknown set = image of the fine one (bore, stair-stepped cone, exit lip, dielectric flange, electrodes represented on every level by the operator, not by a re-classified mask); operator-dependent (Alcouffe-Dendy collapsed-stencil) interpolation from each level's own stencil, with the lumped mass of a solid parent transferred to the surviving parent at the concave stair-step corners so that constants are exactly preserved on every pure-Neumann row (without it a 0.45/cycle slow mode sat on the cone of channel-33 and plume-50); restriction = transpose; Galerkin coarse operators P^T A P (symmetric 9-point; symmetry checked to 1e-11 at build); recursion stops at <= 1024 unknowns, the coarsest operator is inverted densely once on the host (307-752 unknowns on the production grids, <= 4.5 MB)
poisson_gmg_v1.cycle: V(2,2) damped Jacobi omega 0.8, fused residual-and-restrict, FIXED count 14 (default), warm start from the previous potential; one fixed kernel sequence of 12 + 14 x ((levels - 1) x 6 + 1) launches (278 channel-33, 362 plume-v2.0-50, 446 plume-v2.1-33) captured inside the step graph (graph replay bitwise vs the direct launches over 100 steps, tested); float64 throughout; deterministic (no atomics; fixed summation order)
poisson_gmg_v1.contract_and_fail_closed: the same contract as every field solve: true residual |Q - A phi| recomputed with the MESH conductances (matvec_kernel, independent of the multigrid arrays) <= max(absolute_tolerance, relative_tolerance x |rhs|) = 1e-10 |rhs| in production. It is computed inside the captured step EVERY step and a running maximum of the contract ratio |r|^2 / max(abs^2, rel^2 |rhs|^2) is kept over the sync interval; verify() at every host sync (the existing WarpBlockThomas hook) raises PIC2DConvergenceError if the last residual or the interval maximum misses it. Decision: fail-closed STOP, no per-step fall-back to block-Thomas (a fall-back would need a host synchronisation per step and the direct solver's graph is not resident); recovery = resume from the last checkpoint with a larger mg_cycles, like any gate stop. The path fired once during development (12 cycles on the 360 x 1440 box with a wall-heavy synthetic charge: 2.8e-10 |rhs|) and stopped the probe.

audit_of_the_v1_4_hook.frequency: nu_an = alpha omega_ce with omega_ce = e|B|/m_e at the electron's position (bilinear node gather): the Bohm-type effective collision frequency (Smirnov et al. 2004 nu_B ~ omega_c/16; Brandt et al. 2016 D_perp = 0.4 kT_e/eB read as nu = 0.4 omega_ce - a selection probability that depends on the local flux density only, as the paper describes)
audit_of_the_v1_4_hook.event_probability: 1 - exp(-nu_an dt) per electron per step (exact Poisson), applied wherever the electron is: the probability follows |B|, so it vanishes at the nulls and peaks at the cusps / pole faces
audit_of_the_v1_4_hook.energy: the event is a pure velocity rotation: |v| conserved to round-off; the energy ledger carries NO term for it, which is correct for an elastic process (the interval residual stays at the collisionless level with the hook on - test)
audit_of_the_v1_4_hook.ledger: count tallied in cumulative.anomalous (macro events; series currents_a.anomalous_collision_rate_per_s = count x W / interval), the axial momentum handed to the 'turbulent field' in pz_collisions (beside the MCC elastic momentum); checkpointed as an extra ledger key
audit_of_the_v1_4_hook.null_collision_budget: NOT part of the MCC null-collision budget: a separate exact-Poisson process drawn from its own seed stream (CPU stream 3, Warp seed-table slot 2) after the push and before the MCC; statistically equivalent to a joint budget to O(nu_an dt x nu_mcc dt) ~ 1e-7 (nu_an dt <= 0.026 at 0.29 T / 1.4 ps / alpha 0.345; nu_mcc dt ~ 1e-5), and the reason alpha = 0 is bitwise the model without the hook
audit_of_the_v1_4_hook.where_it_fell_short: the v1.4 event redirected the velocity ISOTROPICALLY (the MCC isotropic map), which also randomises v_parallel - a pitch-angle scattering that feeds the cusp loss cones directly; Brandt et al. 2016 rotate only the perpendicular velocity so the parallel speed is unchanged. The sealed ext-val bohm-0.4 option was therefore a bracket of the reference's model, not the model (audit section 4.c)

v2_1_0_event_model.name: bohm_perpendicular_rotation
v2_1_0_event_model.rule: v' = v cos(phi) + (b x v) sin(phi) + b (b . v)(1 - cos(phi)) with b = (B_r, 0, B_z)/|B| and phi uniform on [0, 2 pi): the parallel component is invariant, the perpendicular component turns by phi (gyro-phase reset), the guiding centre jumps by 2 r_L sin(phi/2) in the plane perpendicular to B; |B| = 0 is a no-op (the probability is 0 there)
v2_1_0_event_model.implementation: CPU: sensitivity.rotate_about_field / apply_bohm_rotation, dispatched by apply_anomalous_scattering(config, ...) - the isotropic path draws exactly as v1.4 did (recorded runs replay bitwise); Warp: bohm_kernel mode 1 -> rotate_about_field device function with the same operation order (device vs CPU on recovered angles agree to 1e-9 relative - test)
v2_1_0_event_model.diffusion_coefficient: both event models: D_perp = (kT_e/m_e) nu/(nu^2 + omega_ce^2) = (kT_e/eB) alpha/(1 + alpha^2) for a Maxwellian (the velocity autocorrelation <v_x^2> exp(-nu t) cos(omega_ce t) of a gyrating electron whose gyro-phase is reset at Poisson rate nu); the random-walk picture D = <step^2> nu/4 = r_L^2 nu/2 is the small-alpha limit. alpha = 1/16 -> 0.0623, 1/64 -> 0.0156, 0.345 -> 0.308, 0.4 -> 0.345 of kT_e/eB. AnomalousCollisionConfig.diffusion_factor and sensitivity.bohm_diffusion_coefficient_m2_per_s expose it
v2_1_0_event_model.difference_between_the_models: identical D_perp; the isotropic event additionally scatters the pitch angle at the same rate (parallel mobility, mirror trapping / loss-cone filling), so the two closures differ in the cusp physics; the rotation model is the literature model and the one the alpha-series and the ext-val amendment seal
